thread:
sam: Heads-up — SLO alert just fired for hosted-infer (euw1). p99 error rate ~3.8% and timeouts spiking. Customers reporting latency + 502s. infra-bot: Alert posted to #slo-alerts: hosted-infer.euw1 p99_error_rate > 0.5% (3.8%)
kevin: Copy. Any dashboards/queries you already ran?
sam: Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/inf/hosted-infer-euw1 — the spike starts ~4105001100. Quick log query I ran in Loki:
```
{job="ingress"} |= "status=502" or |= "upstream timeout" | json | line_format "${status} ${upstream} ${request_id} ${lat_ms}"
| sort by lat_ms desc | limit 50
```
Sample lines: 
```
status=502 upstream=grpc://infer-node-17 req=abcd1234 lat_ms=12034
status=504 upstream=backend-pool-5 req=efgh5678 lat_ms=4500 upstream_error=deadline_exceeded
status=502 upstream=warm-proxy req=ijkl9012 lat_ms=9800
```
elaine: Seeing many with long lat_ms and upstream=warm-proxy / infer-node-*. Any KV-cache thrash or batcher backlog? Traces look sparse.
oncall: @oncall jumping in — I've restarted the ingress fleet in euw1 around +10m but alerts persist. No recent deploys in last hour.
kevin: Can you run a focused trace query for requests with lat_ms > 2s and missing spans? Query I use: `trace.service:"hosted-infer" AND duration>2000ms` — if sampling dropped we'll see gaps. Also check `ingress->proxy->backend` span counts.
sam: Ran trace query — there's a trace gap for ~22% of affected requests (no backend spans). Looks like the gateway accepted but never reached the backend or backend failed to start RPC.
elaine: Can you paste the exact failing request headers (small redaction okay)? Might be auth token or size that triggers path.
sam: Example header snippet:
```
{"x-rw-customer":"acme-corp","authorization":"Bearer redacted","content-length":"409600"}
```
kevin: Noticing larger content-lengths in samples. Could be a tail-batching issue causing oversized requests to hold resources and time out. Any burst from a single customer?
sam: Top customer pattern: 43% of 502s are from same org (acme-corp). Trying to repro with their payload now.
elaine: If you can repro, run this curl against the proxy with increased debug: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer redacted" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @payload.json https://euw1.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — capture tcpdump on ingress node.
oncall: I've collected tcpdump from ingress-12 while we repro. Sharing pcap to /tmp/euw1-ingress12.pcap (secure internal).
sam: Repro attempt: sending same 400KB payload repeatedly — after ~8 concurrent requests, proxy starts returning 502 and upstream connection resets. Stack: ingress->warm-proxy->infer-node. Warm-proxy logs show `rpc: connection reset by peer` followed by timeouts.
kevin: Sounds like backend pool exhaustion / keepalive handshake fail. Check warm-proxy max_conns and keepalive settings; also kernel ephemeral port exhaustion on infer nodes?
elaine: I'll look at warm-proxy metrics (conn_count, active_streams) and infer-node OOM/kill logs. If keepalive failing, we might see `handshake timeout` in backend logs.
sam: Metrics: warm-proxy conn_count spike to 1800 (limit 2000), active_streams ~1200, queue_latency rising. infer-node fd_count and process load high but no OOM yet.
oncall: For immediate mitigation, consider short-circuiting acme-corp traffic to a lower-QPS bucket or apply per-tenant concurrency cap. Can we pin a fallback model with lower resource usage?
kevin: Agreed. I'll open a canary route to divert acme-corp to fallback-model-v1 and throttle to 10 rps. @sam can you add an ingress header rule for that tenant?
sam: On it — adding header-route for `x-rw-customer: acme-corp` -> fallback-model-v1 and throttle policy. Pushing now.
elaine: Meanwhile, I'm checking kernel tcp stats on infer nodes for TIME_WAIT / ephemeral port shortage: looking at `ss -s` and `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`. If we see port churn we should tune keepalive and reuse.
kevin: Follow-up actions: 1) Evict acme-corp to fallback (in-flight) 2) Increase warm-proxy max_keepalive_timeout temporarily 3) Add ephem port metrics alert 4) Postmortem if we confirm batching/large payload exacerbates resource exhaustion.
sam: Eviction rule deployed — traffic routed to fallback. Error-rate dropping in grafana now (p99 error down to 0.9%). Keeping watch. :eyes:
elaine: Nice. I'll keep digging into warm-proxy logs for handshake error counts and attach timeline to the incident.
oncall: Thanks team. If error-rate stays below SLO after diversion, we'll notify support and coordinate mitigations with acme-corp. Assigning follow-ups in incident board. :white_check_mark:
